title: Took vg-paradigms release 2026.10.16 by its auto subscription
body:
The dry run broke nothing: no rule it would newly break, no license it would block. What moved:
- ~ checks.commands: A project's commands come first from a proper build environment: its build tool (cargo, uv, bun) in a runtime pinned by the language's own files (rust-toolchain.toml, .python-version, packageManager). What that doesn't cover is, in order of preference: a custom CLI (the most portable, a Rust project's `cargo xtask`), idempotent shell scripts (the least effort), or Nix commands. No task runner (just, make) sits between. The project declares each check as a tend test or gate with the command it runs, which the hooks, agents, other machines and release checks run. A flake's dev shell is optional (system libraries, or a project that's Nix anyway): commands run inside it with its environment cached until flake.nix or flake.lock changes. `nix flake check` is for outputs that are Nix themselves (machine configurations, NixOS VM tests).
- guidance changed
